------
CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE ANIL KUMAR CHOUDHARY ------
For the Petitioner : Mr. J. P. Jha, Sr. Advocate For the State : Mr. Suchendra Prasad, Addl.P.P. For the O.P. No.2 : Mr. Sidhartha Roy, Advocate ------
Order No.07 Dated- 22/03/2023 Heard the parties.

Learned counsel for the opposite party No.2 submits that since the opposite party No.2 has filed Criminal Revision No.12 of 2019 challenging the same order which is sought to be quashed in this Criminal Miscellaneous Petition i.e. order dated 16.02.2019 passed in Complaint Case No.39 of 2018 contending in the said criminal revision that the learned Magistrate ought to have taken cognizance for the offences punishable under Sections 406, 420, 384, 120 B and 506 of the Indian Penal Code as well.

Hence the order which is sought to be quashed in this Criminal Miscellaneous Petition, has not reached finality and in this respect, learned counsel for the opposite party No.2 draws the attention of this Court to the observation in paragraph- 7 by a co-ordinate Bench of this Court in Cr.M.P. No.2872 of 2022 dated 24.01.2023.

Learned senior counsel appearing for the petitioner submits that the observation made by the coordinate bench is a passing remark and not even an obiter dicta let alone ratio decidendi and further, submits that the of Criminal Revision No.12 of 2019, itself is not maintainable as the same has been filed against an interlocutory order.

In view of the submissions made at the Bar, the following two points of law are formulated to be addressed by the rival parties:-
Ranjit Das @ Dr. Ranjeet Das vs The State Of Jharkhand & Another ... ... on 22 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/103612967/
1 (i) Whether the pendency of a Criminal Revision against an order taking cognizance by a Magistrate on the ground that the Magistrate ought to have taken cognizance of some more offences as well, amounts to the order passed by a Magistrate taking cognizance, has not reached finality?

entities.text: Ranjit Das @ Dr. Ranjeet Das vs The State Of Jharkhand & Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
(ii) Whether the pendency of a Criminal Revision before the Court of session,
challenging the order of taking cognizance by the Magistrate, on the ground that the Magistrate ought to have taken cognizance of some more offences as well, will be a bar for exercising jurisdiction under Section 482 Cr.P.C. by the High Court in respect of prayer for quashing the cognizance order of the Magistrate taking cognizance for some of the offences and the entire criminal proceeding?

Both the learned counsels pray for time to address this Court to the points of law formulated today by this Court.
Prayer for time is allowed as the last chance.

The interim relief granted to the petitioner earlier vide order dated 20.11.2019 shall continue till 19.04.2023 but it is made clear that no time will be granted to either of the parties on 19.04.2023.
